results.summary: AtomNPU is a compact 4-bit neural processing unit that performs multiply-accumulate operations for neural network computations. It takes 4-bit input activations and 4-bit weights and produces a quantized output. The design is intended to be tested with a step-by-step guide, though the provided documentation is minimal. No external hardware is specified, and the design is notable for being a minimal NPU implementation.

This is a 4x4 structural array multiplier that multiplies two 4-bit binary numbers using full adders to sum partial products. It is tested via a provided Python testbench where inputs and expected outputs are set. The design requires no external hardware and is a straightforward educational project demonstrating binary multiplication.

This is a 4x4 structural array multiplier that multiplies two 4-bit binary numbers using full adders to sum partial products. It is tested via simulation with a testbench covering five test cases including minimum and maximum values to verify carry propagation. The design requires no external hardware and is a straightforward educational project demonstrating binary multiplication.

This is a 4x4 structural array multiplier that multiplies two 4-bit binary numbers using full adders to sum partial products. It is tested by applying input pairs covering typical, edge, and corner cases, and verifying the 8-bit product. The design requires no external hardware and is a straightforward educational project demonstrating binary multiplication.

The Morse Code Keyer converts a keyed CW input from a straight key or iambic paddle into Morse code tones and a 7-segment character display. It supports iambic modes A and B, adjustable speed from 7 to 110 WPM, and outputs auxiliary dit/dah signals for radio equipment. It requires external paddles and a radio interface, and includes a companion PCB design. The design is notable for its comprehensive feature set and warning against direct radio TX control.

This is a true random number generator that uses a noise source sampled by a digital circuit and conditions the data with SHA-256 to produce cryptographic-quality random numbers. It supports raw entropy and hashed output modes, with built-in health tests, and transmits results via UART. It requires a UART terminal and optionally an oscilloscope for debugging. The design is notable for its cryptographic conditioning and health monitoring.

Bitty is a 16-bit simple processor that communicates via UART. It has pins for UART receive and transmit, and baud rate selection. The design does not require external hardware as UART communication is emulated in the testbench. The documentation is minimal, providing only a one-line description and pin names, so details of its architecture and instruction set are not available.

This is a minimal perceptron-based branch predictor that reads branch instruction addresses and ground truth directions via SPI and outputs predictions. It is based on a research paper and uses latch-based memory, with a functional simulation in C++ and CocoTB tests. It requires external hardware to drive inputs and read outputs, and is notable for its use of a perceptron model and detailed debugging features.

This is a time-to-digital converter with an SPI interface, based on a previous ALU design. It includes pins for SPI communication and start/stop signals, and outputs a busy signal. The documentation is very thin, referring to an external GitHub repository for testing details. No external hardware is required, but the design's functionality and testing are not well described.

This is a 4x4 structural array multiplier that multiplies two 4-bit binary numbers using full adders to sum partial products. It is tested by applying different input combinations and comparing outputs to expected results. The design requires no external hardware and is a straightforward educational project demonstrating binary multiplication.
